releaseNotes: Routing-depth audit fixes: the taste filter was an island. quality-lens.md's Anti-Generic Checks were reachable only by loading the design domain directly, so ad creative, screenshots, and UGC video all cleared a virality score and a design-token check before spend with nothing that asked whether the result looked generic. paid-user-acquisition.md, ugc-creator-engine.md, and app-store-listing-prep.md now cross-link to it, design-visual-system.md's own Taste step now names this skill's reference instead of only an external repo, and the Design Room gate gained one machine-checkable slice of the checklist: a warning when the primary and accent tokens sit within 12 degrees of the same hue, the single-brand-color-at-different-opacities look the checklist names directly.

Three workflows could dispatch before the state they actually depend on existed, even though the catalog's own lane graph said they should wait. Premium mobile craft — the workflow governing haptics, press states, and motion, i.e. taste in the code itself — had no dependency at all and was eligible from the first tick of a run, before a spec or Design Room state existed. The backend data contract could harden before Design Room output existed, and GEO/SEO could publish a page before analytics existed to measure it. All three now depend on the workflow their lane implies they should.

Fixed a miscited command: engineering-orchestration.md told a live launch to run `npm run launchbench` to catch motion craft that was cited in a spec but never applied to shipped code — that command lints the skill's own scenario definitions and has no app-side equivalent, so the one safety net built for this exact failure never actually checked a shipped screen. The on-device verification loop now closes with a taste pass instead of stopping at "it runs," and the engineering plan now carries a per-screen premium-craft requirement alongside the copy-deck one it already had. Also closed: App Store screenshot requests silently dropping the design domain's HTML-proof contract, ad campaigns targeting a Custom Product Page never seeing Apple's numeric ceilings, a documented drift between the human and machine change-cascade maps, and a push-notification file that never pointed at the copy-quality self-check every sibling file already uses.

A safety-net test for the session runner's own liveness — proving a lock's heartbeat keeps refreshing even when the work running under it never calls in — had a tolerance so tight it sometimes failed on nothing but a pause. Node's own timer is best-effort, not guaranteed to the millisecond, and a slow tick on a busy host could put a passing run only a few hundred milliseconds outside the window the test allowed — an outcome that looked identical to a real break, though the lock's actual refresh mechanism, which carries no such tight budget in production, was never at fault. The test now samples more heartbeats over a longer run and allows a tolerance an order of magnitude looser than the fastest real refresh interval, wide enough to absorb ordinary scheduling jitter while still catching the failure it exists to catch: the timer not firing at all. Confirmed clean across three consecutive runs, two of them concurrent to force the exact contention that used to trip it.
